name: Living Server Beta 1.1: The Realm Talks Back
body:
### The realm talks back

Living Server is a free add-on that makes shadowofze's single-player Offline DAoC feel like a live 2003 server. Beta 1.0 gave the bots an endgame. **Beta 1.1 gives them a voice, a memory and a social life**, and adds a one-click Setup for people starting from nothing.

It's for Offline DAoC **0.37 and 0.37b**, with or without the **0.37c** new client.

We aren't going to list everything that happens. Keep /faction open.

### What's new

- **The bots talk.** About 34,000 lines and 393 /faction scenes. Ask "why?" or "where?" after a bot's line and that bot answers. Tells carry on as conversations.
- **They only say what's true.** If a bot says the mids are at a keep, they are. News of keeps, relics and raids is real, and so are the rumours.
- **They remember.** Group with a bot and it remembers you. Bots remember each other too, for better and for worse.
- **The realm has a social life.** /faction fills up the way it did in 2003: the good, the bad and the deeply annoying. Some bots have history with each other that plays out over days, and you can get involved. Do something worth talking about and the realm will talk about it.
- **Not every raid goes to plan.**
- **Names like a 2003 server.** Three in four bots get a name a 2003 player might have picked. The rest get names from their realm's lore.
- **The first half hour counts.** Something worth seeing starts early in every session, not hours in.
- **One-click Setup.** It installs Offline DAoC and Living Server from nothing, or adds Living Server to the game you have.

Every part has its own switch in the launcher's Living Server tab. If you'd rather know everything up front, the full list is in [docs/LIVING-SERVER.md](https://github.com/chris4aker/OfflineDAoC-LivingServer/blob/main/docs/LIVING-SERVER.md) (spoilers), and GMs can set any of it off with `/lstest`.

### The work behind it

#### Writing a 2003 server's voice

- **Era rule:** every line belongs to the game as it stood from launch (9 October 2001) to patch 1.65 (8 October 2003), the last patch before Trials of Atlantis. A validator rejects anything later: Atlantis, artifacts and master levels, New Frontiers towers, Catacombs classes.
- **Period slang, dated by source:** terms come from the Camelot Herald's guides and jargon pages, period forum threads and glossaries. Terms that only show up later (FTW, l2p, imba, "toon") are kept out.
- **Written new:** forums gave the topics and the arguments; no post is copied, and no real player, guild or developer is named.
- **Chosen for the moment:** each line is picked by realm, class, level, zone, what's happening and the bot's personality, so a level 12 Midgard healer doesn't sound like a level 50 Albion tank. Each realm argues its own lore in its own voice.
- **Checked against the world:** before a bot names a place, a keep, a relic or a raid, the server checks it's real.

#### Researching the names

- **The sample:** about 700 real character names, some 300 of them from 2001-2004. They come from two full guild rosters (one dated July 2002) and threads on FreddysHouse, Quarter to Three, AnandTech, the Straight Dope boards and Usenet.
- **What they looked like:** 294 were tagged by hand. About half were made-up single names, with a median of six letters. About 15% were English compounds, 14% jokes and 9% everyday first names. Taken names got a letter doubled.
- **The rules of the time:** Mythic's naming policy, and what role-playing servers renamed.
- **The mix:** the 2003 shares make up 75%, with 25% lore names from each realm's own languages. xX and number names come in at about 3% each. DAoC's own filter took letters only, but they were the era's gamer names everywhere else.
- **Kept out:** memes and jokes from after 2003, famous and Arthurian names, and any name copied from the research.
- **One guard:** no name is a common English word (checked against about 40,900), so "anyone got an axe?" never goes to a bot called Axe.
- **The write-up:** [docs/research/BOT-NAMES-2003.md](https://github.com/chris4aker/OfflineDAoC-LivingServer/blob/main/docs/research/BOT-NAMES-2003.md).

#### Pacing it for a real evening

- **The problem:** in play tests, the best moments came too rarely in a normal evening.
- **The fix:** a session now starts when you log in or come back after half an hour away. The first moments are timed to land within about 30 minutes, and storylines come about twice as often as before.

#### Tracking down the lag (issue #25)

- **The report:** Krolgosh-web reported lag spikes with a large population and diagnosed them.
- **The cause:** bots walking to a far frontier medallion merchant re-proved up to 18 multi-zone routes every 15 seconds, so the server tick stalled for about a second.
- **The fix:** bots now look for a spot within 2,000 units and wait 30 seconds before trying again. A two-day test with up to about 1,000 bots showed no route stalls in the logs.

#### Fixes from the community

- **From shadowofze's unreleased 0.38 work:**
  - Caer Sidi's horsemen and Galladoria's Olcasgean start for bot raids;
  - siege healers raise their dead;
  - Odin's Gate door loops are fixed.
- **From other forks:**
  - an effect leak that slowed long sessions (rambodolphin13);
  - siege timers that never ran (found by stefanrows' fork);
  - healers that restarted cures (stefanrows, via rambodolphin13);
  - low-power Animists, and medallion merchant waits (rambodolphin13);
  - fewer failed routes, and bots that react to attacks like players (stefanrows);
  - quests that can be finished, quest markers and epic chains in order (lometur's HearthDAoC).

#### And more

- A new loading screen and welcome art, a desktop shortcut with its own icon, and the Living Server tab second in the launcher.
- Rezzes:
  - an expired rez offer no longer cancels the next one;
  - a bot no longer raises you into a live fight.
- Groupmates come along through `/tele`, portals and releases, and talk in /group.

### Install

**New to Offline DAoC, or have 0.36 or 0.37 already:**
1. Download `LivingServer-Setup-1.1-beta.exe` and run it.
   - It downloads the game with shadowofze's own downloader when you have nothing.
   - It updates a 0.36 game to 0.37 with his official updater, keeping your saves.
   - It then adds Living Server.
2. A first install turns every Living Server feature on at our suggested settings. Untick the option to choose for yourself. A game that already has Living Server keeps its own choices.
3. Windows SmartScreen may say "Windows protected your PC", because the exe isn't code-signed. Click More info, then Run anyway.

**Prefer doing it by hand:** close the server, launcher and game. Unzip `OfflineDAoC-LivingServer-1.1-beta.zip` into your game folder and run `INSTALL.cmd` from the `LivingServer-1.1-beta` folder. It checks your game, backs up every file it replaces and verifies each copy.

**Have Beta 1.0?** Either way updates it in place. Your characters, bots, guilds, memories and settings stay. `ROLLBACK.cmd` puts every original file back.

Real loot, the Realm Exchange, stablemaster routes and bots that earn their armor are untouched.

### How it was checked

- **Automated:**
  - 4,093 server tests on every build;
  - launcher tests and Windows installer tests (PowerShell 5.1 and real downloads from shadowofze's releases).
- **Played:** two days on a test install with up to about 1,000 bots online.
  - Every Living Server part was seen working in game, along with the new names in the world.
  - Automatic raids opened in all three realms, including a dragon kill that took 56 bots.
  - A 9.5-hour overnight run showed no errors from this code.

### Known issues (it's a beta)

- **Not yet seen in game:** three fixes to raid and storyline moments came after the last play test.
- **Smaller rosters:** automatic raids open only with 80 free level-50 bots in a realm, so they rarely come. A roster filled only with the Lv.1 and Lv.50 buttons has no bots between levels 20 and 49 until they level up.
- **Sieges:** their timers now really run (they were off before), so sieges end, march and repel where earlier builds didn't. Watch them.
- **Hard bosses:** Darkness Falls, Legion and the other level 70+ bosses are still won on numbers. Their special mechanics aren't scripted for bots.
- **Bots don't fall when they die:** the game client keeps a dead pose only for players. A fix was tried and left out of this release.
- **More:** the full list is in [docs/KNOWN-ISSUES.md](https://github.com/chris4aker/OfflineDAoC-LivingServer/blob/main/docs/KNOWN-ISSUES.md). Every change, with its numbers,
